newsitem.title: UK: Gilts end higher on U.S. retail sales, UK RPI data.
newsitem.headline: Gilts end higher on U.S. retail sales, UK RPI data.

text.p: UK gilts ended 17/32 higher on Thursday, boosted by subdued U.S. retail sales data and signs UK inflation was in check.
"The indicators have been very positive for gilts today," CIBC chief economist David Coleman said.
"The market got a boost from some very subdued U.S. data, and a further shot in the arm from a good performance by the U.S. bond market."
The September gilt futures contract closed 17/32 higher at 113-19/32 after earlier reaching an intra-day high of 114-08.
U.S. retail sales for May fell for the third month in a row, dropping 0.1 percent to a seasonally adjusted $210.3 billion, after revised declines of 0.9 percent in April and 0.3 percent in March.
Market expectations had centred on a rise in May sales of 0.4 percent.
UK May retail price data were at the top end of expectations, with RPI rising 2.6 percent year-on-year or 0.4 percent month-on-month. The increase was mainly due to an increase in housing costs.
"The numbers were a little disappointing given hopes that sterling's strength would lead to a further decline in underlying inflation," Union Plc UK economist Philip Shaw said.

The market shrugged off Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown's announcement of a 2.5 percent annual underlying inflation target (RPIX), with the proviso that Bank of England Governor Eddie George would have to provide an explanatory letter if inflation deviated by more than one percentage point in either direction.
The spread to bunds remained steady at 144 basis points, but off the 148-level seen earlier in the week.
